structure_rules.rule: Every coding research task must include web search before implementation planning.
structure_rules.reason: The workspace user explicitly requires web-first work and current external verification.

structure_rules.rule: Coding research must use at least three distinct non-other source types, including one authoritative and one practical or adoption source type.
structure_rules.reason: Single-source research is fragile and can miss implementation trade-offs.

structure_rules.rule: Coding research must record technology_stack, technology_official_docs, and stack_version_constraints; known major technologies such as Spring Boot, C, React, and Next.js require their own official docs or standards.
structure_rules.reason: Different languages and frameworks have different official APIs, standards, runtime constraints, and migration risks.

structure_rules.rule: Coding research must compare at least two language or runtime options, select one explicitly, and record maintainability-focused decision notes.
structure_rules.reason: The easiest implementation language is not always the easiest language to maintain across tooling, tests, ecosystem, runtime constraints, and project boundaries.

structure_rules.rule: Coding research must inspect and record high-signal issue/discussion/community sources when available, including Stack Overflow, Reddit, GitHub Issues/Discussions, and project forums.
structure_rules.reason: Practical issue threads and high-engagement discussions reveal repeated problems, stale answers, migration friction, and edge cases that official docs may not emphasize.

structure_rules.rule: Before implementation, inspect relevant open-source repositories, reference implementations, or well-structured code and record code_reference_sources plus code_reference_notes.
structure_rules.reason: Source-code-writing agents need concrete structure and implementation examples, not only docs or summaries.

structure_rules.rule: Before writing source code, compare best-practice architecture frameworks, reference architectures, and well-structured source architectures; record architecture_reference_sources, architecture_options, and architecture_decision_notes.
structure_rules.reason: Source code should be shaped by proven architecture options and explicit trade-offs, not only local implementation convenience.

structure_rules.rule: Architecture research must separately record theory/formal sources and practitioner opinion sources, then explain convergence, disagreement, and local trade-offs before choosing structure.
structure_rules.reason: Architecture theory, cloud/reference frameworks, and high-signal practitioner discussions can disagree; treating them as separate evidence roles prevents false certainty.

structure_rules.rule: Coding research must compare at least two folder-structure options and record folder semantics so maintainers can infer purpose and ownership by inspecting the tree.
structure_rules.reason: Folder structure is part of maintainability; unclear folder names and unrecorded ownership create repeated rediscovery cost.

structure_rules.rule: Research outputs must record reference_config_paths pointing to the configs used.
structure_rules.reason: Future review needs to know which source rules shaped the decision.

structure_rules.rule: When coding research uses large-company engineering blogs, official research labs, architecture centers, or high-signal independent sources as seeds, include enterprise-source-registry.json in reference_config_paths.
structure_rules.reason: The user wants these high-quality site lists managed separately and traceably.

source_selection_rules: Start with web search before local planning.
Check enterprise-source-registry.json when the task benefits from large-company engineering, research-lab, architecture-center, or high-signal independent sources.
Check source-discovery-registry.json when broader global, Korean, Indian, paper, or Korean local review source origins are useful.
Use Naver Map, Kakao Map, Naver Blog/Search, official pages, and _tools/korean-local-review/ when Korean user behavior or local-market review signals affect implementation.
Use at least one current official or primary source when external behavior matters.
Record technology_stack and check stack-specific official docs or standards for each major known technology, such as Spring Boot, ISO C, React, and Next.js.
Record stack_version_constraints with exact versions, standards, compatibility ranges, runtime assumptions, or explicit unknowns.
Compare at least two language or runtime options and record selected_language plus language_decision_notes before implementation.
Language selection must prioritize maintainability, testability, ecosystem maturity, runtime constraints, available tooling, and project boundary fit.
Search high-signal issue/discussion sources when available, including Stack Overflow high-vote or accepted answers, Reddit discussions, GitHub Issues/Discussions, and project forums.
Record issue_discussion_sources, issue_discussion_notes, and community_signal_notes so community signals are separated from factual proof.
Use open-source source material when implementation behavior, maintenance, or license matters.
Before writing source code, look for best-fit architecture patterns, reference architectures, and well-structured source architectures.
Separate architecture_theory_sources from architecture_practitioner_sources so formal guidance and high-signal practitioner opinions can disagree without being collapsed into one truth.
Compare at least two architecture options and record why the selected structure fits the current scope, quality attributes, and project boundary.
Record architecture_tradeoff_notes with theory-vs-practice disagreements, convergence points, and local validation needs.
Compare at least two folder_structure_options and record folder_structure_decision_notes before creating or reshaping folders.
Record folder_semantics_notes so top-level and important nested folders are understandable by inspection.
Record maintainability_notes that connect the selected language, architecture, and folder structure to future change cost.
Inspect relevant open-source repositories, reference implementations, example applications, and tests before writing source code.
Record code_reference_sources and code_reference_notes so implementation choices can be traced back to concrete code examples.
Record architecture_reference_sources, architecture_options, and architecture_decision_notes so source-code structure can be traced back to architecture evidence.
Record source_value_provenance and plan_evidence so source values, assumptions, recommendations, and validation choices can be audited.
Use papers, standards, or technical reports when methodology, risk, or security claims matter.
Use technical blogs, analysis articles, community signals, social signals, and contrary examples to discover trade-offs and adoption signals.
Treat popularity and social signals as discovery or adoption signals, not proof.
Validate internal knowledge with knowledge-skeptic-agent before relying on it.
